meaning: Each tie names the phrase of the paper that a Lean declaration states, as read side by side for Proof Reader (wcook04/proof-reader 3858afbe00b2, papers/navier-stokes-appendix-b). Titles, reading notes, topics and comparisons are AI-drafted or AI-assessed; no mathematician has reviewed them.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).

notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectEnt: The pin flux uses the skew derivative of each compact pin generator. Its divergence agrees with the required pin Laplacian up to a gradient term, whose pairing with a divergence-free perturbation vanishes.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded: The distinct label is the entire triple consisting of helical component, temporal frequency and azimuthal order. Amplitudes with the same triple must be added before taking their squared norm, so the budget retains their cross terms.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialData: The four fields represent the vectors Gⱼ and Uⱼ, the matrix for Fⱼᵀ and the scalar qⱼ. Derivative maps use output-component rows and differentiation-direction columns, so their matrices are transposed relative to the paper’s written gradient convention.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialNorms: The numerical budgets for ∇Uⱼ and Fⱼ use the Frobenius norm, whereas the analytic decay bounds use operator norms. A freely chosen decay constant can absorb norm equivalence; a fixed numerical budget must satisfy its specified norm bound.
notes.Breakdown.AdjointDefect.RemainderDualBou: The dual conclusion records spatial integrability for almost every time and integrability of the resulting scalar time pairing. Joint absolute integrability follows from a separate weighted-norm argument after the finite harmonic amplitudes have been shown to supply a finite |y|R norm.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.isExtendedCert: The newly chosen witness is a common decay bound. The certificate retains the supplied profile, period, multiplier, pins, adjoints, parameter family and numerical budgets.
notes.Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.shiftValid_of_: There are exactly two discrepancy fields: the difference between the frozen and central profiles, and the displacement across the parameter set. Their gradient estimates use L² and L³, respectively, with the corresponding distinct constants.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Ad: The general adjoint argument permits fitted directions with individual potentials. This cell construction requires that fitted set to be empty, leaving the centre potential and the free-direction terms of B.12.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is: The finite frame is indexed by actuator first and adjoint second: its (l,j) entry is the coefficient of β_l in Vⱼ·β. The enclosures use a closed ball; changing to the paper’s open ball changes only a sphere of measure zero.
The target is required to equal the pin values of the approximate profile for every parameter. Consequently the target gap in the generic certificate is identically zero for this cell construction.
notes.Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Of: An off-diagonal quadratic coefficient already contains both ordered terms. The final sum runs only over i≤l, counting each off-diagonal pair and each diagonal term once.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.treeState_ho: Local moments and the corresponding global coordinates can differ by gauge and constant-pressure shifts. The cell forms are required to ignore those shifts, preserving their quadratic values for every allowed choice of free coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.patchGradSq: For azimuth k, the rectangle test-gradient energy is |∂rφ|²+|∂zφ|²+k²|φ|²/r². The last term is part of the Dirichlet bound even though the test polynomial is represented on the meridional rectangle.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.complexCo: The real and imaginary contributions of a complex loss column are counted as two indexed real columns. They may be dependent or zero; their count still bounds the possible dimension lost to the negative squares.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.stateTerm: The finite-dimensional argument allows the prescribed coordinates to change by a fixed linear function of the free coordinates and removes the pressure coordinates ignored by the quadratic form. This gives the general version of the paper’s physical/free-coordinate decomposition.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartCoord: The radial variable is σ=|y|/(L+|y|). A period-one time variable elsewhere in the formulas is independent of this compactified radius.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionR: A radius depending on direction must also be measurable, constant along positive rays and bounded between one positive lower bound and one finite upper bound. These are the geometric hypotheses used to extend the ray estimate to weak perturbations.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.hessTailGain: The coefficient-tail norm and the physical energy with measure r dr dz have different radial factors. In the coefficient normalisation the Hessian gain is r* times the first omitted polynomial eigenvalue, plus (k₀−2)₊²/r₂, where r*=r₁ off the axis and r*=1 on an axis cell.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.pointwiseQua: A certified lower bound for the curl-gradient coefficient may be negative even though the actual coefficient is nonnegative. The scalar argument handles that case explicitly and also permits a zero diagonal in the final two-by-two quadratic test.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip: The lattice reflection is ι↦(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). Under (j,n)=(2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁), it becomes (j,n)↦(j,−n), preserving temporal frequency and reversing azimuthal frequency.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic: A paper label ι corresponds to temporal frequency 2ι₂−ι₁ and azimuthal frequency κι₁. Every mode set and frequency-dependent coefficient must be read using this same conversion.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointSizeBound: The two alternatives bound the spatial L³ or L² norm of the adjoint. The L² alternative pairs with the perturbation’s uniform-norm estimate and its constant S(w*)=[2π(2√w*)]⁻¹ᐟ².
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff: The L³ adjoint bound has coefficient 2/(√3 w*). The L² adjoint bound uses the perturbation’s uniform estimate and has coefficient S(w*)/√w*, where S(w*)=[2π(2√w*)]⁻¹ᐟ².
notes.Breakdown.CoerciveWeak.pieceMultiplierDe: The positive and negative parts of each whole mode density and of the stretching term are integrated separately, allowing infinite positive integrals. Once the negative part is finite, the multiplier comparison also makes the positive part finite and permits the subtraction used in B.20.
notes.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.rows: The represented rows and their nonnegative weights are stored separately. Multiplying each row by the square root of its weight gives the paper’s seminorm [F]² as a sum of squared row pairings.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialSeri: The radial flux joins across radial interfaces and the polar flux across polar interfaces. These normal-component joins supply the weak divergence used in integration by parts, while the permitted tangential jumps do not introduce additional surface terms.
